title: John Howard Program Management and Data Collection System
summary: A privacy-minded Windows application shaped around nonprofit program workflows, controlled information transfer, and reporting, with test evidence kept synthetic.
problem: Program teams need software workflows for managing programs and relevant participant information while supporting controlled transfers to the main office and privacy-conscious funder reporting.
role: Led discovery, requirements, planning, design, and technical decisions; built and maintained application test coverage.
currentStatus: Synthetic-data prototype and implementation foundation approaching MVP. It is not deployed or production-approved.
publicationBoundary: Public examples use synthetic data only. No real participant data or internal client material is authorized for this portfolio.
limitations: No approved public demo or sanitized repository is available yet.
The prototype is not deployed or production-approved.

claimPolicy: Describe the system as active development approaching MVP, never as deployed or production-ready.

evidence: Translated stakeholder discussions, feedback, mockups, and requirements into testable workflows.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The work is for the John Howard Society of Saint John. The Windows desktop system is intended to support program management, relevant participant information, controlled transfers to the main office, and privacy-conscious funder reporting.

sections.heading: Role and approach
paragraphs: I led discovery, requirements, planning, design, and technical decision-making. Stakeholder discussions, feedback, mockups, and requirements were turned into workflows that could be built and tested.
bullets: Organized workflows around program staff and main-office needs.
Kept the system's publication boundary explicit while planning evidence and tests.

sections.heading: Implementation and verification
paragraphs: The application is built with C# and WPF. Verification includes automated coverage across unit, integration, view-model, UI-structure, and regression layers, alongside manual test evidence using synthetic data.

sections.heading: What is public today
